name: Gum Tragacanth Wafers
description: Historical recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Soak gum tragacanth in water twenty-four hours and rub through a fine wire sieve; add enough confectioners' sugar to knead.
Flavor with a few drops of oil of wintergreen.
If liked pink, color with fruit red.
Roll until very thin on a board or marble dredged with sugar.
Shape with a small round cutter or cut in three-fourths inch squares.
Spread wafers, cover, and let stand until dry and brittle.
This mixture may be flavored with oil of lemon, clove, sassafras, etc., and colored as desired.

source.author: Fannie Merritt Farmer
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak gum tragacanth in water twenty-four hours and rub through a fine wire sieve; add enough confectioners' sugar to knead.
2. Flavor with a few drops of oil of wintergreen.
3. If liked pink, color with fruit red.
4. Roll until very thin on a board or marble dredged with sugar.
5. Shape with a small round cutter or cut in three-fourths inch squares.
6. Spread wafers, cover, and let stand until dry and brittle.
7. This mixture may be flavored with oil of lemon, clove, sassafras, etc., and colored as desired.
